SHIELD module · The seven elements

Corporate compliance

The seven elements of an effective compliance program, maintained rather than written once and filed.

Get your free compliance review See all of SHIELD

The OIG does not ask whether you intended to run a program. It asks for the records the program produced.

What it covers

  1. 01
    Compliance hotline

    Anonymous reporting, available online and on a toll-free number, so a concern has somewhere to go that is not a manager.

  2. 02
    Exclusion monitoring

    Screened monthly against the LEIE, SAM and state Medicaid lists. Employing an excluded individual is a per-claim liability.

  3. 03
    Compliance committee meetings

    Scheduling and documentation automated, so the minutes exist without anybody chasing them.

The seven elements

The Office of Inspector General defines what an effective compliance program requires. This module is where all seven are maintained.

  1. 01Written policies and procedures
  2. 02Compliance leadership and oversight
  3. 03Training and education
  4. 04Lines of communication
  5. 05Enforcing standards
  6. 06Risk assessment, auditing and monitoring
  7. 07Response and corrective action

Questions about corporate compliance

Why does exclusion monitoring need to be monthly?

Employing an excluded individual creates liability on every claim their work touches, and exclusion lists change continuously. Monthly screening against the LEIE, SAM and state Medicaid lists is what keeps that from accumulating quietly.

Does the hotline have to be anonymous?

An effective programme needs a route that does not run through somebody’s manager. Reports can be made anonymously, online or on a toll-free number.

Is this sold separately from SHIELD?

It is part of SHIELD rather than a separate product. SHIELD is the system of record; this is one of the four modules inside it, and the evidence it produces lands in the same place as everything else.

How fast can we be up and running?

Most organizations are fully live in two to three weeks. Your advisor does the heavy lifting: policy customization, staff roster, training assignment. Your team spends about three hours in total.
